articles.title: JRC study examines AI’s occupational impact in the generative era
articles.description: A new European Commission Joint Research Centre study finds that AI exposure has increased substantially across all occupational categories in the European labour market.
articles.content: The paper traces AI exposure from 2008 to 2024 by linking 352 AI benchmarks to 14 cognitive abilities, 108 work tasks and 127 occupations. It finds the strongest exposure in information-processing and problem-solving abilities, with comparatively high-skilled occupations more exposed than elementary occupations, indicating a broad labour-market impact.

fr.title: Une étude du JRC examine l’impact professionnel de l’IA à l’ère de l’IA générative
fr.description: Une nouvelle étude du Centre commun de recherche de la Commission européenne montre que l’exposition à l’IA a fortement augmenté dans toutes les catégories professionnelles du marché du travail européen.

de.title: JRC-Studie untersucht die Auswirkungen von KI auf Berufe im Zeitalter der generativen KI
de.description: Eine neue Studie der Gemeinsamen Forschungsstelle der Europäischen Kommission zeigt, dass die KI-Exposition in allen Berufsgruppen auf dem europäischen Arbeitsmarkt deutlich gestiegen ist.

es.title: Un estudio del JRC analiza el impacto de la IA en el trabajo en la era de la IA generativa
es.description: Un nuevo estudio del Centro Común de Investigación de la Comisión Europea muestra que la exposición a la IA ha aumentado considerablemente en todas las categorías profesionales del mercado laboral europeo.

it.title: Uno studio del JRC analizza l’impatto dell’IA sul lavoro nell’era dell’IA generativa
it.description: Un nuovo studio del Centro comune di ricerca della Commissione europea mostra che l’esposizione all’IA è aumentata notevolmente in tutte le categorie professionali del mercato del lavoro europeo.

pt.title: Estudo do JRC analisa o impacto da IA no trabalho na era da IA generativa

nl.title: JRC-studie onderzoekt de impact van AI op werk in het tijdperk van generatieve AI

articles.title: Mistral AI partnership with China’s Z.ai raises questions for EU tech sovereignty
articles.description: A reported partnership between French AI company Mistral AI and Chinese infrastructure provider Z.ai highlights the difficulty European firms face in securing sufficient domestic compute capacity.
articles.content: The arrangement illustrates a tension at the centre of Europe’s technology-sovereignty strategy: European AI companies need large-scale computing, but the available supply chain remains globally dependent. For policymakers and businesses, the development reinforces the importance of the EU’s planned cloud, AI and gigafactory measures.

articles.title: Italy’s Domyn raises over $1 billion (mostly debt) for sovereign AI and Colosseum supercomputer
articles.description: Milan-based Domyn secured more than $1 billion in financing, predominantly debt, to advance its sovereign AI models and the Colosseum AI supercomputer in southern Italy.
articles.content: Only about one-tenth of the package is equity. Domyn (formerly iGenius) focuses on mission-critical, regulated-sector AI and is leading the European Commission’s Frontier AI Grand Challenge consortium ‘Europa’. The company is building Colosseum with Nvidia hardware, targeting models above a trillion parameters and positioning European organisations to retain control over models, data and infrastructure.

articles.title: EU approves Spanish consortium for AI Gigafactory bid in Móra la Nova
articles.description: The European Commission cleared a joint venture of ACS, Telefónica, Banco Santander and Spain’s SETT to compete for one of the planned AI Gigafactories, with a primary site planned in Móra la Nova, Tarragona.
articles.content: The public-private consortium, also involving Multiverse Computing and a small stake for the Catalan government, aims to mobilise up to €5 billion for advanced AI compute infrastructure. articles.title: Danish AI infrastructure startup Velatir raises €5M seed to expand across Europe
articles.description: Odense-based Velatir secured €5 million in seed funding to scale its European-owned AI control and infrastructure platform that helps companies manage AI usage, security and compliance.
articles.content: The round was co-led by Spintop Ventures and Ugly Duckling Ventures, with participation from Norrsken Evolve, angels including n8n founder Jan Oberhauser, and a matching loan from Denmark’s EIFO. Velatir’s platform provides visibility and guardrails across AI tools, agents, employees and infrastructure while running exclusively on European-hosted systems, positioning it for data sovereignty and AI Act compliance needs.

articles.title: Germany’s Flip raises €22 million to scale AI platform for frontline workers
articles.description: Stuttgart-based Flip secured €22 million from Notion Capital, HV Capital and L-Bank to expand its AI-native employee experience platform for deskless and frontline workforces.
articles.content: The funding will support AI infrastructure and knowledge tools aimed at the large share of employees who do not work at desks. Flip already serves major industrial and retail customers across production, logistics, retail and care. The company emphasises bringing AI capabilities to frontline roles that have so far seen limited adoption compared with office environments.

articles.title: ECB President Lagarde warns Europe cannot afford to miss the AI transition
articles.description: Christine Lagarde warned that fragmented European markets and finance are limiting the ability of European firms to scale in artificial intelligence.

articles.description: New guidance clarifies who must comply with Article 50 transparency obligations for interactive AI systems and AI-generated content.
articles.content: The guidelines explain disclosure duties involving interactions with AI, deepfakes, public-interest text without human review, and certain biometric or emotion-recognition systems. They support the transparency rules that began applying on 2 August 2026.
